sentences.text:
======
 Appearance:
 MR K L PANDYA, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Applicant(s) No.
 1  RULE NOT RECD BACK for the Respondent(s) No. 1 - 2  =============================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P.P.BHATT  Date : 18/07/2017  ORAL ORDER 1.

The present application is moved by the applicant-State seeking leave to appeal under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 challenging the judgment and order of acquittal dated 09.09.2016 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Kathor, in Criminal Case No.774 of 1999, wherein at the end of trial, the learned Judge was pleased to acquit the respondents-opponents for the offence under Sections 2(1-A)(A), (1-A)(M) as well as Sections 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

2. On perusal of the material placed on record and upon hearing the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, it becomes clear that the sample was collected on 16.06.1995 and three bottles of "Mixed Pickle" were seized from the shop of the respondents and the same were sent for Public analyst,
Bhuj/Surat.

Thereafter, the sanction for prosecution was granted by the authority on 20.02.1999 and accordingly, the HC-NIC Page 1 of 2 Created On Sun Aug 20 06:28:54 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/11801/2017 ORDER complaint was filed on 26.05.1999.
Thus, apparently there is substantial and gross delay in filing of the complaint.
The gross delay in filing of complaint is not even properly explain by the complainant.

sentences.text: 1 3. On perusal of the judgment and order passed by the learned Trial Court, it appears that the learned Court below has taken into consideration oral as well as documentary evidence produced on record.

On perusal of the discussion made by the learned Court below in paragraph 10 while discussing point no.1, it appears that the learned Court below after careful consideration of the evidence on record has also considered the question of law discussed in the case of State of Gujarat versus Nanjibhai Kurjibhai Hirpara reported in 2012 (2) FAC 280 as well as in the case of State of Gujarat versus Kaushikkumar J. Doshi reported in 2007(2) FAC 190 and reached to the conclusion that this is a fit case wherein benefit of doubt is require to be given to the present respondents.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the learned Court below has passed and order of acquittal by giving benefit of doubt to the respondents.

4. The findings recorded by the learned Court below are based on the evidence and there is no infirmity in the said findings, and therefore, this Court is of the view that leave to appeal is not required to be granted in the instant case.
Hence, the application for leave to appeal is rejected.
Accordingly, present application stands disposed of.
